analysis:
Examined three benchmark and profiling script changes, all offline developer tooling outside the provider runtime, coordinator WebSocket, attestation, key custody and cache-storage boundaries in the threat model.

1. scripts/gemma_contbatch/validation.py line 16: the accepted raw schema versions for 'scheduler prefill' widen from (3,4) to (3,4,5). Validation still enforces the model ID, finite values, a complete TTFT sample matrix and positive timings (validate_scheduler, lines 86-107). This only admits a reviewed newer raw-output schema version in a benchmark comparison tool. It does not touch the secrets, keys, authorization or at-rest cache behavior in the threat model, and I see no regression.

2. scripts/gptoss_profile/summary.py lines 68-70: summarize_cell now copies prefillChunkTokens and maxBatchedTokensPerStep from the report with .get(), so a missing key yields None. These are numeric engine-geometry values written to summary.json. No new input parsing, subprocess call, path handling or sensitive data is added. The summary still runs validate() before summarize_cell (lines 107-108), and the raw SHA-256 is still checked (lines 105-106). Nothing sensitive is added to the output.

3. scripts/gptoss_profile/tests/test_integrity.py lines 101-115: a new unit test covers both the new fields and the legacy-report fallback to None. It is test-only code.

T-041 and the cache threat definitions are not affected: no cache TTL, key derivation, salt scoping, disk budget or gate logic changed. Remaining integration questions: the Swift emitter of the new report fields and the scheduler-prefill schema v5 are outside the supplied evidence, but they carry no security conclusion here.
